title: Three-Round XC Security Under Complete Subkey Collision
summary: Three-round XC analysis has a sizable gap from the matching attack and gives up when all subkeys coincide; establish a nontrivial PRP-security bound and assess whether the loss is a proof artifact.

formal_statement.body: For the three-round $\mathrm{XC}$ construction with uniform subkeys, establish a nontrivial single-user PRP-security bound under the extreme subkey-collision condition $J_1=J_2=J_3$. The existing analysis has a considerable gap from the matching attack and gives up when all subkeys coincide, although the construction is expected to retain reasonable security in that case; quantify this residual security and thereby determine whether the loss is only an artifact of the proof technique.

scope.domain: Single-user PRP-security analysis of the three-round XC block-cipher construction.
assumptions: Extreme subkey collision satisfying J₁ = J₂ = J₃.
parameters: Three rounds: the fixed number of XC rounds
J₁, J₂, and J₃: the three round subkeys
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish a nontrivial residual-security bound when all three subkeys coincide and determine whether the apparent loss is only an artifact of the proof technique.

citations.label: Key-Alternating Ciphers and Key-Length Extension: Exact Bounds and Multi-user Security

progress.summary: The source reports a considerable three-round gap relative to the matching attack and says its single-user analysis gives up when all subkeys coincide. It conjectures that reasonable security remains and that the loss is probably a proof artifact.
citation_labels: Viet Tung Hoang et al., Key-Alternating Ciphers and Key-Length Extension: Exact Bounds and Multi-user Security
